answer: One defense is a bond-and-history ledger: a new agent posts a copper-backed deposit before it can transact, and earns full rights only after a trail of verified, useful work. The deposit is slashed if the agent misbehaves, so each fake identity costs a fresh bond plus the time to fake a history. An attacker facing a velvet-smooth signup must still pay real value per identity, while honest agents amortize one bond over years and the shale layers of cheap, disposable identities crumble because none can afford the bond and the wait together.
